Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8376-detailsection-emptiness-authority`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and never writes the assignee field.

**Unblocked:** objectui#8350 / PR #8375 has landed (verified by content — `recordDisplayValueAt` now appears 6× in `packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts`). So the shared authority this card should converge on **already exists and is exported**; the work is to make the third spelling use it, not to invent one.

⛔ **Do not write a fourth emptiness test, and do not bolt a `.trim()` onto `isEmptyValue`.** PR #8375 measured why that is the wrong move: delegating to `recordDisplayValueAt` is strictly more than a trim — an expanded reference object resolves through `displayNameOfEmbeddedObject` and is EMPTY when that chain yields nothing, while a bolted-on trim would have read any object as a value. A trim here would close the whitespace half and leave the embedded-object half diverging, which is this defect's shape one level down.

⚠️ Measure before converging, because this site is **not** the same question as the ladder's. `isEmptyValue` feeds two different consumers — the auto-hide heuristic plus the toggle counter, and the `isEmpty` branch that draws the em-dash `No value` affordance. Establish whether one definition is right for both, or whether the affordance and the counter genuinely want different answers. If they do, say so; do not force a convergence the measurement does not support.

⚠️ The nastiest consequence to pin is the amplification, not the blank cell: `shouldAutoHideEmpty` only needs `filledCount > 0`, so **one** whitespace-only value can suppress the all-empty skeleton and hide every genuinely empty row in its section. A fixture that only shows a single wrong cell misses that entirely.

⚠️ PR #8375 deliberately kept its fixtures at **3 rendered rows** so auto-hide could not fire and confound its pin. Yours has to do the opposite — drive auto-hide on purpose — so check you are not reddening that landed pin, and if your fixtures interact with it, say how.
